sourceEvidence.explanation: Every role other than ADMIN or an instructor alias is normalized to STUDENT, so SUPER_USER and unknown persisted roles inherit student semantics.
Any non-Admin actor passes when its persisted JSON permission array contains the requested permission; no SUPER_USER or unknown-role ceiling exists.
The activity boundary consumes the unsafe normalized role and determines eligibility from institute membership without an explicit role allowlist.

independentEvidence.impact: A SUPER_USER or unknown role can be treated as a student and can obtain legacy permissions through persisted permission injection, including activity and server-side capabilities outside oversight.
independentEvidence.recommendation: Implement a fail-closed recognized-role resolver, keep SUPER_USER outside legacy managed roles, reject UNKNOWN, and enforce a hard SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN ceiling before parsing payloads, resource access, execution or writes. Add independently reviewed unknown-role and injected-permission cases.

independentEvidence.title: Inline server actions authenticate but do not authorize role, institute or course ownership

sourceEvidence.explanation: The callable action checks only that a session exists, then creates an ActivityTemplate using the closure courseId.
The action checks only authentication before accepting hidden tests and creating a template.
The action checks only authentication, then creates or updates SyllabusItem and ActivityTemplate records without verifying teaching role, institute, course assignment or template ownership.
The action performs JSON parsing and a database create after authentication alone.
The action creates a template for the closure courseId after only a session-presence check.
The action creates a template after authentication alone, with no persisted role/assignment/scope check.

independentEvidence.impact: Direct or replayed server-action requests can let any authenticated actor, including SUPER_USER, create or modify assessment templates, syllabus records and hidden-test material. Page redirects do not protect callable actions.
independentEvidence.recommendation: At each inline action, authenticate and then require a recognized teaching/Admin role, selected institute, persisted course assignment and child ownership before parsing attacker-controlled content or writing. Verify all six through genuine compiled-action replay tests with valid inputs and side-effect fingerprints.

independentEvidence.title: Proposed pathname-marker shell gate is not yet proven trustworthy for Next RSC and action traffic

sourceEvidence.explanation: Current middleware forwards static and _next requests without a marker, forwards API requests independently, and supplies no server-derived pathname marker.
The design depends on a middleware-overwritten request marker but leaves normalization, rewrites, RSC/action requests and fail-closed behavior for later independent review.

The current layout authorizes cross-institute access only for ADMIN and mounts the generic DashboardLayout after performing eligibility, course and gamification reads; it has no SUPER_USER route allowlist.

independentEvidence.impact: A spoofed, absent, stale or internally rewritten marker could permit legacy dashboard rendering or deny legitimate RSC navigation. The generic layout can query and serialize unrelated state before a proposed child-page guard runs.
independentEvidence.recommendation: Do not approve the marker design until exact middleware request-header replacement and layout parsing are specified for document, prefetch, RSC, refresh, rewrite and server-action requests. Fail closed before legacy data fetching. Prefer route-group isolation or another server-derived mechanism if the marker cannot be demonstrated trustworthy.

independentEvidence.title: Retained title and instructor-name metadata lacks a content-classification boundary

sourceEvidence.explanation: The amendment redacts descriptions and announcement content but deliberately retains course, event and material titles plus instructor names, while deferring adequacy assessment.
Course.title, SyllabusItem.title and CalendarEvent.title are unrestricted stored strings without a public/safe classification.
Marker checks detect only seeded restricted strings; the frozen fixtures use benign titles and do not establish semantic safety for production titles or names.

independentEvidence.impact: Student names, grades, answers or other restricted information embedded in retained titles can appear in oversight JSON, RSC payloads and the shell despite empty description fields.

Either introduce an approved safe-summary source/classification or redact affected strings and revise the exact heading/fixture expectations. independentEvidence.title: Mandatory access-audit failure behavior exists only as a proposal

sourceEvidence.explanation: The existing helper performs a single insert, but no supplied oversight service or response boundary exists to prove that data is withheld when the insert fails.
Fail-closed audit behavior is selected architecturally but explicitly remains future implementation and testing.
The proposed audit-failure suite is marked NOT_EXECUTED and its supplementary test file does not yet exist.

independentEvidence.title: Cookie/Bearer actor-selection semantics are not yet verified at protected boundaries

sourceEvidence.explanation: A valid cookie wins; an invalid cookie falls through to Bearer. This is deterministic but requires boundary tests to prove that actor identity, permissions and ownership are never mixed.
The server helper similarly prefers the cookie and falls back to the Authorization header, including transitional raw session-id lookup.
The only explicit conflicting-token verification is a future test in a file that does not exist and is marked NOT_EXECUTED.

independentEvidence.impact: Without implemented and reviewed edge coverage, different handler/action helpers may select different actors from the same request, potentially combining a SUPER_USER cookie with a privileged Bearer token or vice versa.
independentEvidence.recommendation: Adopt and document one canonical precedence rule, use the same resolver at each HTTP/action boundary, and test valid/valid, valid/invalid, invalid/valid, expired, inactive and transitional-id combinations while asserting one actor supplies role, permissions and ownership.

independentEvidence.title: Boundary inventory is broad, but proposed verification can pass without operation-level completeness

sourceEvidence.explanation: The inventory declares 120 route files, 20 action files and a sensitive gradebook service, spanning many verbs and exports.
A single future test title claims every inventoried HTTP handler and another claims exported actions, but the mapping contains no machine-readable per-route/per-method/per-export case list.
Harness validation checks nonempty test and coverage labels, not that each inventoried operation has an assertion.
The gate requires named security coverage but does not compare a boundary inventory against executed per-operation results.

independentEvidence.impact: A loop can omit a route verb, alias, inline action or callable skill and still produce a passing named test and coverage label. Normal-role regressions may likewise be sampled rather than exhaustive.
independentEvidence.recommendation: Bind the reviewed inventory digest into the plan and supplementary tests. Emit one result per route-method, action export, inline action and callable service; fail on omissions, duplicates, import failures or validation-only responses. Include explicit normal-role positive and negative expectations for affected boundaries.

independentEvidence.title: Current generic shell leaks and mutates out-of-scope account and academic state for SUPER_USER

sourceEvidence.explanation: Every role other than an instructor alias or ADMIN receives the student navigation set.
Unknown roles, including SUPER_USER, fall through to adminTabs.
Unknown roles receive admin items, while profile and settings links are always rendered despite the resolved login/logout/own-identity-only exception.
Settings, NotificationBell, profile, privacy and help controls are mounted for non-Admin roles, including SUPER_USER.
Mounting the bell fetches academic notification messages and exposes a PATCH mutation.
The layout calculates activity/KX eligibility and reads a gamification profile before mounting the generic shell.

independentEvidence.impact: Before the dedicated shell is implemented, SUPER_USER can receive student/Admin navigation, academic notifications and unsupported profile/settings controls; merely visiting the shell performs unrelated reads and exposes mutation paths.
independentEvidence.recommendation: Branch to a dedicated server-selected AcademicOperationsShell before any legacy eligibility, enrollment, gamification or notification work. Render only scope selection, oversight navigation, own identity and logout, and directly deny the underlying unsupported APIs.
